title: Functions: parameters, results, and contracts
lead: Separate validation, computation, and presentation so a small function can be checked without a console.
why: Duplicating code duplicates defects. A function names an operation and defines a responsibility boundary, but it helps only when inputs, outputs, and side effects are clear.
objectives: Justify: Pure computation and side effects
Implement and verify the lab against its exact contract.
Identify a common defect: Do not assign result before every check succeeds. Do not return a reference to a local variable.
prerequisites: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.while-do-while. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

concepts.definition: an observable change beyond the return value.
an expression supplied in a function call.
a local input name in a function declaration.
an obligation before performing an operation.
a guarantee after an operation whose preconditions hold.

sections.title: Calls and definitions
paragraphs: In int twice(int value), twice names the function, the first int is the return type, and value is a local parameter. The body runs when called, not when the compiler encounters its definition. return 2*value finishes this invocation and supplies its result to the caller.

Define a teaching function before main so its declaration is visible at the call site. int result=twice(4) supplies the argument 4 and stores the result 8. Calling it does not print anything by itself; output is a separate operation.

sections.title: Values, references, and const
paragraphs: An int value parameter receives a separate value: changing it does not change the caller’s int. int& binds to the original object and permits mutation. const int& prevents mutation through that reference but neither copies the object nor makes it permanently const.

Small scalar values are usually passed by value. Larger read-only objects can use const references. In the lab, const std::string& checks a string without copying it. A reference must not outlive its owner; never return a reference to a local variable.

sections.title: Preconditions and postconditions
paragraphs: The twice contract bounds its input so 2*value fits the type. That is straightforward for -1000 through 1000, but not for arbitrary int. A precondition is the caller’s obligation; a postcondition is the guaranteed result property when that obligation holds.

Do not treat malformed external input as a violation that can be ignored. At the boundary, main checks extraction and ranges before an internal function receives values. For an expected rejection, a bool result with an explicitly documented output parameter is useful.

sections.title: Pure computation and side effects
paragraphs: A calculation function should not secretly read cin or change a global accumulator. The same arguments yield the same result without changing the environment. A unit test can then pass arguments directly and compare the result without replacing the console.

An output reference makes mutation visible in the signature but needs an exact rule: leave it unchanged on false. Calculate into a temporary and assign only on success. This is a simple form of operation atomicity.

sections.title: Decomposition without unnecessary coupling
paragraphs: Split the task into validation, calculation, and presentation. Each function should answer one question and have a meaningful name. Avoid ten unrelated parameters when one value suffices; a later struct will group related data.

Local variables in separate calls are independent. Returning a result by value is safe; returning a local object’s address is not. Recursion, authored templates, and overloading are unnecessary here and are not hidden lab requirements.

sections.title: Testing a function separately from input
paragraphs: Build an argument table: lower boundary, a normal value, upper boundary, and nearby rejections. Check that read-only operations leave the original object unchanged and that a false result preserves the output parameter.

Then add integration cases for cin: empty input, a wrong type, and an extra token. A successful unit test does not establish parser correctness. Next, pass a whole sequence to a function using the standard span view.

workedExamples.title: Copy and mutation
workedExamples.purpose: A copied parameter and a reference parameter have different mutation effects.
steps: original starts at 4. Calling copied(original) creates a separate parameter value=4; result initialization is not complete yet.
++value changes the parameter from 4 to 5. original is still 4 because the parameter is a copy.
return value yields 5. The call ends and result is initialized to 5. The first output line is 4 5.
changed(original) binds its int& parameter to original. There is no separate copied integer here.
++value now changes original from 4 to 5. result stays 5. The second output line is 5.
For your own prediction, start at original=10: expect 10 11, then 11. Explain each state before running.

workedExamples.title: Rejection without mutation
workedExamples.purpose: A negative width must not mutate a previously established result.
steps: result starts at 17. checkedArea(-1,2,result) checks width first: -1 is outside 0..1000.
return false ends this call before assigning result. ok is false and result remains 17; output is 0 17.
checkedArea(3,4,result) passes all bounds. result becomes 12 and the call returns true; output is 1 12.
A CLI line invalid alone cannot show that result stayed 17. This direct call observes both the returned bool and the output parameter.

experiments.title: Predict before running
experiments.action: Trace the first worked example step by step, then run all of its cases.
experiments.prediction: A signature communicates what a function reads, returns, and changes.
experiments.verification: Compare every state transition and stdout; record a mismatch as a hypothesis rather than revising the expectation afterward.

experiments.title: A counterexample to a wrong rule
experiments.action: Using the second example and theory, construct a minimal safe case for this defect: Do not assign result before every check succeeds. Do not return a reference to a local variable.
experiments.prediction: The correct and incorrect models should make distinguishable predictions without executing undefined behaviour.
experiments.verification: Preserve the prediction, actual output, and an explanation of the violated rule.

steps: Restate the input, output, and rejection contract in your own words.

Start from the scaffold, implement the valid path, then add boundary checks.
